Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
curated_comment: Confirmed 0 (no change). Breen 1981 3.2.4: personal pronouns inflect NOMINATIVE (= subject of any clause: S and A) vs ACCUSATIVE (object): nom ngayu 'I' (ex.63-65) vs acc ngana 'me' / -nta (ex.66-67). S=A!=P => nominative-accusative, i.e. NOT ergative alignment on pronouns. Classic Pama-Nyungan Silverstein split.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
curated_comment: Confirmed 0 (no change). Pronouns are nominative-accusative (Breen 1981: 3.2.4): nominative = S and A, accusative = O (ex.66-67). S=A!=P, not ergative.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
curated_comment: Confirmed 0 (no change). Same nominative-accusative pronoun paradigm (Breen 1981: 3.2.4, 3.2.6). No ergative flagging on pronouns. Silverstein split.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
curated_comment: Confirmed 1 (no change). Breen 1981 3.2.3: full NPs show absolutive (unmarked) for S and O vs ergative -ngkV/-tV for A; e.g. erg panya-ngka 'woman-ERG' (ex.32) with unmarked O/S. S=P!=A => ergative flagging on full NPs. PROVENANCE: re-anchor citation - in this v2 the nominal ergative is pp.40-41 (ex.32/34/35), not p.38/ex.22; pronoun citation p.46 is correct. Examples are largely Ngawun; confirm Mayi-Kulan attestation where it matters.
